summary: SpaceX successfully launched 27 Starlink satellites to orbit from California, while civil space operations monitor the impending re-entry of NASA's Swift space telescope as it prepares to fall back to Earth. In military and space security developments, civil and defense satellites are expanding planetary defense efforts by tracking atmospheric fireballs to protect Earth against asteroid threats, while the Department of the Air Force announced a flu vaccine requirement for many Guardians, Airmen, and civilian employees. In propulsion technology, researchers have introduced a new gel fuel that could enhance control systems for future rocket and satellite maneuvers. Scientific investigations also yielded new findings: analysis of spacesuit material suggests Mars dust may prove less abrasive than lunar dust, while detected heavy hydrogen in object 3I/ATLAS's methane indicates a frigid birthplace. Furthermore, astronomers continue to analyze a highly reflective lava world and unexplained atmospheric activity surrounding the star Betelgeuse. Looking ahead, stargazers can watch for a notable planetary alignment overnight on November 1–2, when the moon, Mars, and Jupiter will appear together in the constellation Leo.
